key_insight: Micropillar compression shows that in anorthite, mechanical twinning is easier than slip, with twinning CRSS near 300 MPa and slip strength strongly decreasing with temperature.
engineering_relevance: These results improve constitutive modeling of plagioclase-rich crustal rocks by quantifying temperature-dependent plasticity and the relative activation stresses of key deformation mechanisms.
method: FIB-milled ~1 μm micropillars from three crystal orientations
Uniaxial compression inside SEM at 25, 300, and 800 °C
Measured yield stress/CRSS for twinning and multiple slip systems
evidence_signal: The study tested 36 pillars and found twinning CRSS around 300 MPa with little sensitivity to temperature or strain rate, while slip-oriented pillars softened markedly as temperature increased.
watch_item: Micropillar results capture small-scale single-crystal behavior and may not fully translate to polycrystalline crustal conditions or long-term geologic deformation.
paper_title: Quantification of plastic deformation in anorthite using micropillar compression
